claim: Human TFIID is a megadalton-sized complex comprising TATA-binding protein (TBP) and 13 TBP-associated factors (TAFs).
source: Human TFIID is a megadalton-sized complex comprising TATA-binding protein (TBP) and 13 TBP-associated factors (TAFs).
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and is supported by established scientific knowledge about TFIID composition.

claim: TBP binds to core promoter DNA, recognizing the TATA-box.
source: TBP binds to core promoter DNA, recognizing the TATA-box.
evidence: This is a well-established fact in the field, supported by prior research.

claim: A ternary complex is formed by TBP and the histone fold (HF) domain-containing TFIID subunits TAF11 and TAF13.
source: We identified a ternary complex formed by TBP and the histone fold (HF) domain-containing TFIID subunits TAF11 and TAF13.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by experimental data including SEC, native MS, and AUC.

claim: TAF11/TAF13 competes for TBP binding with TATA-box DNA.
source: We demonstrate that TAF11/TAF13 competes for TBP binding with TATA-box DNA, and also with the N-terminal domain of TAF1 previously implicated in TATA-box mimicry.
evidence: This is demonstrated by band-shift assays and SEC experiments showing DNA release upon TAF11/TAF13 binding to TBP.

claim: The architecture of the TAF11/TAF13/TBP complex was determined using an integrative approach combining crystal coordinates, biochemical analyses and data from cross-linking mass-spectrometry (CLMS).
source: In an integrative approach combining crystal coordinates, biochemical analyses and data from cross-linking mass-spectrometry (CLMS), we determine the architecture of the TAF11/TAF13/TBP complex, revealing TAF11/TAF13 interaction with the DNA binding surface of TBP.
evidence: This describes the methodology used in the study.

claim: TAF11/TAF13 interacts with the DNA binding surface of TBP.
source: In an integrative approach combining crystal coordinates, biochemical analyses and data from cross-linking mass-spectrometry (CLMS), we determine the architecture of the TAF11/TAF13/TBP complex, revealing TAF11/TAF13 interaction with the DNA binding surface of TBP.
evidence: This is supported by HDX-MS data, CLMS data, and the structural model.

claim: A highly conserved C-terminal TBP-interaction domain (CTID) exists in TAF13.
source: We identify a highly conserved C-terminal TBP-interaction domain (CTID) in TAF13, which is essential for supporting cell growth.
evidence: This is supported by sequence alignments and mutagenesis experiments.

claim: The C-terminal TBP-interaction domain (CTID) in TAF13 is essential for supporting cell growth.
source: We identify a highly conserved C-terminal TBP-interaction domain (CTID) in TAF13, which is essential for supporting cell growth.
evidence: This is demonstrated by cell growth experiments in yeast showing that mutations in this domain arrest cell growth.

claim: Eukaryotic gene expression is a highly regulated process controlled by a plethora of proteins arranged in multiprotein complexes including the general transcription factors (GTFs), Mediator and RNA polymerase II (Pol II).
source: Eukaryotic gene expression is a highly regulated process which is controlled by a plethora of proteins, arranged in multiprotein complexes including the general transcription factors (GTFs), Mediator and RNA polymerase II (Pol II) (Gupta et al., 2016; Thomas and Chiang, 2006).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Regulated class II gene transcription is initiated by sequential nucleation of GTFs and Mediator on core promoter DNA.
source: Regulated class II gene transcription is initiated by sequential nucleation of GTFs and Mediator on core promoter DNA (Buratowski and Sharp, 1990).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation.

claim: TFIID is a cornerstone in the transcription initiation process and links cellular signaling events with regulatory DNA elements and the components of the transcription machinery.
source: The GTF TFIID is a cornerstone in this process and links cellular signaling events with regulatory DNA elements and the components of the transcription machinery (Albright and Tjian, 2000).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: A basal transcription system which supports initiation can be reconstituted with TBP and GTFs TFIIA, TFIIB, TFIIE, TFIIF and TFIIH in vitro.
source: A basal transcription system which supports initiation can be reconstituted with TBP and GTFs TFIIA, TFIIB, TFIIE, TFIIF and TFIIH in vitro (with TFIIA not essential if TBP repressors are not present in the system); however, TFIID is required to respond to activators (Hampsey and Reinberg, 1999).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation.

claim: TFIIA is not essential for basal transcription if TBP repressors are not present in the system.
source: A basal transcription system which supports initiation can be reconstituted with TBP and GTFs TFIIA, TFIIB, TFIIE, TFIIF and TFIIH in vitro (with TFIIA not essential if TBP repressors are not present in the system); however, TFIID is required to respond to activators (Hampsey and Reinberg, 1999).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation.

claim: TFIID is required to respond to activators.
source: A basal transcription system which supports initiation can be reconstituted with TBP and GTFs TFIIA, TFIIB, TFIIE, TFIIF and TFIIH in vitro (with TFIIA not essential if TBP repressors are not present in the system); however, TFIID is required to respond to activators (Hampsey and Reinberg, 1999).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation.

claim: In mammalian cells, the promoters of virtually all protein-encoding genes are occupied by TFIID.
source: In mammalian cells, the promoters of virtually all protein-encoding genes are occupied by TFIID, and loss of TFIID components causes embryonic lethality (Gegonne et al., 2012; Kim et al., 2005; Mohan et al., 2003).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Loss of TFIID components causes embryonic lethality.
source: In mammalian cells, the promoters of virtually all protein-encoding genes are occupied by TFIID, and loss of TFIID components causes embryonic lethality (Gegonne et al., 2012; Kim et al., 2005; Mohan et al., 2003).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: TFIID subunits are thought to mediate cross-talk with epigenetic modifications on nucleosomes and regulatory DNA elements in promoter regions.
source: TFIID subunits are thought to mediate cross-talk with epigenetic modifications on nucleosomes and regulatory DNA elements in promoter regions (Vermeulen et al., 2007; Verrijzer et al., 1995).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: X-ray crystallography revealed many details of TFIID components at near atomic resolution.
source: X-ray crystallography revealed many details of TFIID components at near atomic resolution (Gupta et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: Cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM) provided essential insight into TFIID architecture and promoter DNA interaction.
source: Cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM) provided essential insight into TFIID architecture and promoter DNA interaction (Bieniossek et al., 2013; Cianfrocco et al., 2013; Louder et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: The identification of a discrete TAF-containing complex in the cytoplasm of cells provided first insight into holo-TFIID assembly from preformed sub-modules, regulated by nuclear import mechanisms.
source: The recent identification of a discrete TAF-containing complex in the cytoplasm of cells provided first insight into holo-TFIID assembly from preformed sub-modules, regulated by nuclear import mechanisms (Trowitzsch et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: Canonical human TFIID comprises TATA-binding protein (TBP) and 13 TBP-associated factors (TAFs).
source: Canonical human TFIID comprises TATA-binding protein (TBP) and 13 TBP-associated factors (TAFs) (Matangkasombut et al., 2004; Müller and Tora, 2014).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Non-canonical TFIID and TAF-containing complexes have been identified regulating spermatogenesis and stem cell development.
source: Furthermore, non-canonical TFIID and TAF-containing complexes have been identified regulating spermatogenesis and stem cell development (Goodrich and Tjian, 2010; Maston et al., 2012; Müller et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: A nuclear core-TFIID complex was identified, made up of two copies each of TAF4, 5, 6, 9 and 12.
source: A nuclear core-TFIID complex was identified, made up of two copies each of TAF4, 5, 6, 9 and 12 (Bieniossek et al., 2013; Wright et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Biochemical and structural studies established the histone-fold domain (HFD) as a key TAF-TAF interaction motif within TFIID.
source: Biochemical and structural studies established the histone-fold domain (HFD) as a key TAF-TAF interaction motif within TFIID (Gangloff et al., 2001a).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: TAF3, 4, 6, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12 and 13 contain HFDs and assemble specifically into heterodimers (TAF3-10, TAF4-12, TAF6-9, TAF8-10 and TAF11-13).
source: TAF3, 4, 6, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12 and 13 contain HFDs and assemble specifically into heterodimers (TAF3-10, TAF4-12, TAF6-9, TAF8-10 and TAF11-13) (Birck et al., 1998; Gangloff et al., 2001b; Werten et al., 2002; Xie et al., 1996).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: TFIID recognizes core promoter DNA via its TATA-box-binding protein subunit, TBP.
source: TFIID recognizes core promoter DNA via its TATA-box-binding protein subunit, TBP.
evidence: This is established knowledge in the field.

claim: TBP is central to transcription regulation in eukaryotes and is the only subunit present in the transcription initiation complexes of each of the three RNA polymerases.
source: TBP is central to transcription regulation in eukaryotes and is the only subunit present in the transcription initiation complexes of each of the three RNA polymerases (Koster et al., 2015; Thomas and Chiang, 2006; Tora and Timmers, 2010).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: TBP consists of a highly variable N-terminal domain with less well-understood function and a conserved DNA-binding C-terminal core domain comprising two symmetrical pseudo-repeats.
source: TBP consists of a highly variable N-terminal domain with less well-understood function and a conserved DNA-binding C-terminal core domain comprising two symmetrical pseudo-repeats (Thomas and Chiang, 2006; Tora and Timmers, 2010).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Crystal structures of the conserved TBP core revealed a saddle-like shape with a concave DNA binding surface recognizing the minor groove of TATA-box containing DNA.
source: Crystal structures of the conserved TBP core revealed a saddle-like shape with a concave DNA binding surface recognizing the minor groove of TATA-box containing DNA (Kim et al., 1993; Nikolov et al., 1996; Nikolov et al., 1992).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: The DNA-binding activity of TBP/TFIID is tightly regulated by gene-specific co-factors that can activate or inhibit transcription.
source: The DNA-binding activity of TBP/TFIID is tightly regulated by gene-specific co-factors that can activate or inhibit transcription (Koster et al., 2015; Tora and Timmers, 2010).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: The TFIID component TAF1 was found to associate with the concave DNA-binding surface of TBP via its N-terminal domain (TAF1-TAND), exhibiting TATA-box mimicry.
source: The TFIID component TAF1 was found to associate with the concave DNA-binding surface of TBP via its N-terminal domain (TAF1-TAND), exhibiting TATA-box mimicry (Anandapadamanaban et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: TAF1-TAND, unstructured in isolation, was found to adopt a three-dimensional structure closely resembling the TATA-element in shape and charge distribution when bound to TBP.
source: TAF1-TAND, unstructured in isolation, was found to adopt a three-dimensional structure closely resembling the TATA-element is shape and charge distribution when bound to TBP (Burley and Roeder, 1998; Liu et al., 1998).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: The TAF1-TAND interaction with TBP is conserved in yeast, Drosophila and human.
source: This interaction is conserved in yeast, Drosophila and human (Anandapadamanaban et al., 2013; Burley and Roeder, 1998; Liu et al., 1998; Mal et al., 2004).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: The high-resolution structure of TBP bound to yeast TAF1-TAND revealed anchoring patterns in transcriptional regulation shared by TBP interactors.
source: The recent high-resolution structure of TBP bound to yeast TAF1-TAND revealed anchoring patterns in transcriptional regulation shared by TBP interactors, providing insight into the competitive multiprotein TBP interplay critical to transcriptional regulation (Anandapadamanaban et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: Mot1 is an ATP-dependent inhibitor of TBP/TATA-DNA complex formation.
source: Mot1 is an ATP-dependent inhibitor of TBP/TATA-DNA complex formation (Auble and Hahn, 1993).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation.

claim: Mot1 regulates the genomic distribution of TBP and was shown to influence transcription levels both positively and negatively.
source: Mot1 regulates the genomic distribution of TBP and was shown to influence transcription levels both positively and negatively (Pereira et al., 2003).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: Structural analysis revealed the molecular mechanism of Mot1 wrapping around TBP resembling a bottle opener, with a 'latch helix' blocking the concave DNA-binding surface of TBP and acting as a chaperone to prevent DNA re-binding to ensure promoter clearance.
source: Recent structural analysis revealed the molecular mechanism of Mot1 wrapping around TBP resembling a bottle opener, with a 'latch helix' blocking the concave DNA-binding surface of TBP and acting as a chaperone to prevent DNA re-binding to ensure promoter clearance (Wollmann et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: Mot1 and negative co-factor 2 (NC2) are thought to cooperate in gene-specific repression of TBP activity.
source: Mot1 and negative co-factor 2 (NC2) are thought to cooperate in gene-specific repression of TBP activity (Hsu et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: TFIIA competes with NC2 for TBP.
source: The GTF TFIIA, on the other hand, competes with NC2 for TBP (Kamada et al., 2001; Xie et al., 2000) and promotes TBP/DNA interactions in a ternary TFIIA/TBP/DNA complex, facilitating formation of and stabilizing the preinitiation complex (PIC).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: TFIIA promotes TBP/DNA interactions in a ternary TFIIA/TBP/DNA complex, facilitating formation of and stabilizing the preinitiation complex (PIC).
source: The GTF TFIIA, on the other hand, competes with NC2 for TBP (Kamada et al., 2001; Xie et al., 2000) and promotes TBP/DNA interactions in a ternary TFIIA/TBP/DNA complex, facilitating formation of and stabilizing the preinitiation complex (PIC).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Interaction of TFIIA with TBP results in the exclusion of negative factors that would interfere with PIC formation.
source: Interaction of TFIIA with TBP results in the exclusion of negative factors that would interfere with PIC formation, and TFIIA acts as a coactivator assisting transcriptional activators in increasing transcription levels (Bleichenbacher et al., 2003).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: TFIIA acts as a coactivator assisting transcriptional activators in increasing transcription levels.
source: Interaction of TFIIA with TBP results in the exclusion of negative factors that would interfere with PIC formation, and TFIIA acts as a coactivator assisting transcriptional activators in increasing transcription levels (Bleichenbacher et al., 2003).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: Genetic and biochemical experiments suggested that the TFIIA/TBP/DNA complex is further stabilized by the histone-fold containing TFIID subunits TAF11 and TAF13 conveying the formation of a TAF11/TAF13/TFIIA/TBP/DNA assembly.
source: Genetic and biochemical experiments suggested that the TFIIA/TBP/DNA complex is further stabilized by the histone-fold containing TFIID subunits TAF11 and TAF13 conveying the formation of a TAF11/TAF13/TFIIA/TBP/DNA assembly (Kraemer et al., 2001; Lavigne et al., 1999; Robinson et al., 2005).
evidence: This is based on prior work cited, though the current study contradicts this finding.

claim: TAF11/TAF13 did not stabilize the preformed TFIIA/TBP/DNA complex but resulted in TAF11/TAF13-dependent release of free promoter-containing DNA in band-shift assays.
source: Surprisingly, in our titration experiments, TAF11/TAF13 did not stabilize the preformed TFIIA/TBP/DNA complex but, in marked contrast, resulted in TAF11/TAF13-dependent release of free promoter-containing DNA in band-shift assays (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study demonstrated by band-shift assays shown in Figure 1D.

claim: TFIIAs-c and TAF11/TAF13 did not interact in the experiments.
source: We observed that TFIIAs-c and TAF11/TAF13 did not interact in our experiments (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is demonstrated by SEC experiments shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: Combining the TAF11/TAF13 dimer with TBP revealed a novel TAF11/TAF13/TBP complex that was stable in size exclusion experiments.
source: Combining the TAF11/TAF13 dimer with TBP, in contrast, revealed a novel TAF11/TAF13/TBP complex that was stable in size exclusion experiments (Figure 1E).
evidence: This is demonstrated by SEC experiments shown in Figure 1E.

claim: Human TAF11/TAF13 did not further stabilize the preformed TFIIA/TBP/DNA complex, but rather sequestered TBP from this complex giving rise to a novel assembly comprising TAF11, TAF13 and TBP.
source: We concluded that human TAF11/TAF13 did not further stabilize the preformed TFIIA/TBP/DNA complex, but rather sequestered TBP from this complex giving rise to a novel assembly comprising TAF11, TAF13 and TBP.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data presented.

claim: The ternary TAF11/TAF13/TBP complex remained stable in the presence of excess AdMLP DNA.
source: We tested competition between TAF11/TAF13/TBP formation and TBP binding to AdMLP DNA and showed that the ternary TAF11/TAF13/TBP complex remained stable in the presence of excess AdMLP DNA (Figure 1F).
evidence: This is demonstrated by SEC experiments shown in Figure 1F.

claim: TAF11/TAF13 and TATA-DNA compete for at least parts of the same binding interface within TBP.
source: Thus, our results indicate that TAF11/TAF13 and TATA-DNA compete for at least parts of the same binding interface within TBP, and that once TAF11/TAF13 is bound to TBP, TATA-DNA binding is precluded.
evidence: This is inferred from the competition experiments showing that TAF11/TAF13 binding prevents DNA binding.

claim: Once TAF11/TAF13 is bound to TBP, TATA-DNA binding is precluded.
source: Thus, our results indicate that TAF11/TAF13 and TATA-DNA compete for at least parts of the same binding interface within TBP, and that once TAF11/TAF13 is bound to TBP, TATA-DNA binding is precluded.
evidence: This is inferred from the competition experiments.

claim: TAF1-TAND effectively sequestered TBP from the TAF11/TAF13/TBP complex.
source: We found that TAF1-TAND effectively sequestered TBP from the TAF11/TAF13/TBP complex, evidenced by TAF11/TAF13 eluting in the flow-through fraction. Elution by maltose, in contrast, revealed a TAF1-TAND/TBP complex (Figure 1G).
evidence: This is demonstrated by pull-down experiments shown in Figure 1G.

claim: The TAF11/TAF13/TBP complex has a 1:1:1 stoichiometry.
source: Next, we set out to determine the subunit stoichiometry within the TAF11/TAF13/TBP complex, by using two complementary methods, analytical ultra-centrifugation (AUC) and native mass-spectrometry (native MS). Both methods were consistent in revealing a 1:1:1 complex (Figure 2A,B; Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is demonstrated by AUC and native MS experiments shown in Figure 2A and 2B.

claim: Collision-induced dissociation (CID) in native MS evidenced a TBP monomer and a TAF11/TAF13 dimer.
source: Collision-induced dissociation (CID) in native MS, evidenced a TBP monomer and a TAF11/TAF13 dimer (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is demonstrated by native MS experiments shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Purified TBP evidenced a dimer in the native MS.
source: Of note, our control experiment using highly purified TBP evidenced a dimer in the native MS (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is demonstrated by native MS experiments shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: The ternary assembly accommodates one copy each of TAF11, TAF13 and TBP in the complex.
source: In aggregate, our results are consistent with a ternary assembly which accommodates one copy each of TAF11, TAF13 and TBP in the complex.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the stoichiometry experiments.

claim: HDX-MS results underscored that the DNA-binding surface of TBP was recognized by TAF11/TAF13.
source: The HDX-MS results underscored that the DNA-binding surface of TBP was recognized by TAF11/TAF13, evidenced by decrease in deuteration levels which corresponds to increased protection from the solvent of peptides located in the concave surface of TBP upon TAF11/TAF13 binding.
evidence: This is demonstrated by HDX-MS experiments shown in Figure 2C and Table 2.

claim: The binding of TAF11/TAF13 engages both symmetric pseudo-repeats in TBP, thus spanning the entire concave interface.
source: The extent of protection within TBP further indicates that the binding of TAF11/TAF13 engages both symmetric pseudo-repeats in TBP, thus spanning the entire concave interface (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is inferred from the HDX-MS data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: One peptide (AA residues 157–167) in TBP evidenced an increased level of deuteration upon TAF11/TAF13/TBP complex formation in the HDX-MS experiments.
source: Interestingly, we identified one peptide (AA residues 157–167) in TBP which evidenced an increased level of deuteration upon TAF11/TAF13/TBP complex formation in the HDX-MS experiments (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is demonstrated by HDX-MS experiments shown in Figure 2C.

claim: The peptide at AA residues 157–167 in TBP is located at the dyad relating the two pseudo-symmetric repeats in TBP.
source: This peptide is located at the dyad relating the two pseudo-symmetric repeats in TBP.
evidence: This is based on knowledge of TBP structure.

claim: The increased deuteration of the peptide at AA residues 157–167 in TBP indicates that this particular region within TBP is more protected in a presumed TBP dimer which dissociates when TAF11/TAF13 is binding and the 1:1:1 complex is formed.
source: We interpret this result as an indication, that this particular region within TBP is more protected in a presumed TBP dimer which dissociates when TAF11/TAF13 is binding and the 1:1:1 complex is formed.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the HDX-MS data.

claim: HDX-MS experiments provide direct evidence that TAF11/TAF13 engage the concave DNA-binding surface of TBP.
source: Our HDX-MS experiments provide direct evidence that TAF11/TAF13 engage the concave DNA-binding surface of TBP, in excellent agreement with our above described biochemical experiments involving TAF11/TAF13, TBP, AdMLP DNA and TAF1-TAND.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the HDX-MS data.

claim: The final three-dimensional TAF11/TAF13/TBP ternary complex model accommodated more than 90% of all experimental constraints.
source: Our final three-dimensional TAF11/TAF13/TBP ternary complex model accommodated more than 90% of all experimental constraints and evidenced a tight association of the TAF11/TAF13 histone-fold regions with the concave surface of TBP, giving rise to a compact structure (Figure 3, Figure 3—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 3 and Figure 3—figure supplement 4.

claim: The TAF11/TAF13/TBP ternary complex model evidenced a tight association of the TAF11/TAF13 histone-fold regions with the concave surface of TBP, giving rise to a compact structure.
source: Our final three-dimensional TAF11/TAF13/TBP ternary complex model accommodated more than 90% of all experimental constraints and evidenced a tight association of the TAF11/TAF13 histone-fold regions with the concave surface of TBP, giving rise to a compact structure (Figure 3, Figure 3—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 3.

claim: Alternative calculations using rotated TBP were far inferior in accommodating experimental spatial and distance restraints.
source: To validate our approach, we carried out calculations using alternative starting models. For instance, we rotated TBP by 180⁰ around its axes to artificially expose the convex surface to TAF11/TAF13, or, alternatively, to reverse the location of the N- and C-terminal stir-ups of TBP (data now shown). These alternative calculations were far inferior in accommodating experimental spatial and distance restraints, in addition to being inconsistent with our biochemical data, thus substantiating our TAF11/TAF13/TBP structural model.
evidence: This is stated in the text as a validation of the structural model.

claim: Sequence alignments revealed a very high degree of sequence conservation in the C-terminal TAF13 domain, with key residues virtually identical in all TAF13 proteins analyzed.
source: We analyzed TAF13 primary sequences from yeast to human (Figure 4). Sequence alignments revealed a very high degree of sequence conservation in this C-terminal TAF13 domain, with key residues virtually identical in all TAF13 proteins analyzed (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is demonstrated by sequence alignments shown in Figure 4A.

claim: TAF13 Mutant A, with conserved residues in the center of the TAF11/TAF13/TBP interface substituted with alanine, completely abolished TBP interaction.
source: In Mutant A, we substituted with alanine conserved residues located in the center of the TAF11/TAF13/TBP interface, while in Mutant B we changed conserved amino acid residues located more to the periphery (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A). Both TAF13 mutants readily formed dimers with TAF11. SEC experiments evidenced impairment of TBP interaction with both mutants, but with notable differences. In case of Mutant A, TBP interaction was completely abolished and the TAF11/TAF13/TBP complex was not detected.
evidence: This is demonstrated by SEC experiments shown in Figure 4B.

claim: TAF13 Mutant B, with conserved residues more to the periphery of the interface changed, showed diminished but residual TBP interaction.
source: In case of Mutant B, on the other hand, TBP interaction was likewise diminished, however, residual TAF11/TAF13/TBP complex formation was clearly observed (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is demonstrated by SEC experiments shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Plasmids expressing wild-type or Mutant B Taf13 proteins supported growth at the non-permissive temperature in yeast temperature-sensitive Taf13 mutant strains.
source: While plasmids expressing either wild-type (WT) or Mutant B Taf13 proteins supported growth at the non-permissive temperature (both on solid media and in suspension cell culture at close to wild-type levels), Mutant A did not rescue the lethal phenotype at 37°C, evidencing that the conserved mutations in this mutant effectively arrested cell growth (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is demonstrated by cell growth experiments shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Mutant A did not rescue the lethal phenotype at 37°C in yeast temperature-sensitive Taf13 mutant strains, evidencing that the conserved mutations in this mutant effectively arrested cell growth.
source: While plasmids expressing either wild-type (WT) or Mutant B Taf13 proteins supported growth at the non-permissive temperature (both on solid media and in suspension cell culture at close to wild-type levels), Mutant A did not rescue the lethal phenotype at 37°C, evidencing that the conserved mutations in this mutant effectively arrested cell growth (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is demonstrated by cell growth experiments shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Plasmids expressing wild-type or Mutant B Taf13 proteins supported growth after IAA addition in the Taf13 degron yeast strain, while expression of Mutant A lead to cell growth arrest.
source: We corroborated our results by means of a novel Taf13 degron yeast strain (Warfield et al., 2017). In this strain, endogenous Taf13 is fused to an auxin-inducible degron (AID) tag resulting in Taf13-AID depletion upon addition of a chemical, indole-3-acetic acid (IAA). The plasmids expressing wild-type or Mutant B Taf13 supported growth after IAA addition, while expression of Mutant A lead to cell growth arrest (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is demonstrated by cell growth experiments shown in Figure 4D.

claim: All TFIID subunits tested were equally present in co-IPs of HA tagged wild-type Taf13, as well as Mutant A and Mutant B.
source: Next, we investigated whether the effects we observed could be related to compromised TFIID integrity which may have lost the mutated proteins. We performed co-immunoprecipitations (co-IPs) of hemagglutinin (HA)-tagged wild-type and mutant Taf13 proteins, and used specific antibodies to probe for the presence of Tafs and TBP in our co-IP experiments (Figure 4E). All TFIID subunits tested were equally present in co-IPs of HA tagged wild-type Taf13, as well as Mutant A and Mutant B.
evidence: This is demonstrated by co-IP experiments shown in Figure 4E.

claim: The mutations introduced in TAF13 did not cause noticeable dissociation of Taf13 from TFIID.
source: We conclude that the mutations we introduced did not cause noticeable dissociation of Taf13 from TFIID.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the co-IP experiments.

claim: The amino acids in TAF13 CTID, which when mutated abolish TAF11/TAF13 interactions with TBP, are required for a functional TFIID complex in vivo.
source: Taken together, our observations consistently suggest that the amino acids in TAF13 CTID, which when mutated abolish TAF11/TAF13 interactions with TBP, are required for a functional TFIID complex in vivo.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the mutagenesis and cell growth experiments.

claim: Human TFIID assembly involves preformed cytosolic and nuclear submodules.
source: We recently demonstrated that human TFIID assembly involves preformed cytosolic and nuclear submodules (Trowitzsch et al., 2015), and we now asked whether the human TAF11/TAF13/TBP complex would likewise represent such a sub-assembly.
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: Dimeric TAF11/TAF13 complex was found in the cytosol representing the complete HF pair.
source: To this end, we performed co-immunoprecipitations (co-IPs) from HeLa cell cytosolic and nuclear extracts using an anti-TAF11 antibody (Figure 5). We found dimeric TAF11/TAF13 complex in the cytosol representing the complete HF pair.
evidence: This is demonstrated by co-IP experiments shown in Figure 5.

claim: TBP could not be detected in cytosolic co-IPs.
source: We could not detect TBP in cytosolic co-IPs, however, our experiments evidenced TAF7 association with cytoplasmic TAF11/TAF13.
evidence: This is stated based on co-IP experiments shown in Figure 5.

claim: TAF7 associates with cytoplasmic TAF11/TAF13.
source: We could not detect TBP in cytosolic co-IPs, however, our experiments evidenced TAF7 association with cytoplasmic TAF11/TAF13.
evidence: This is demonstrated by co-IP experiments shown in Figure 5.

claim: The anti-TAF11 co-IP from nuclear extract contained all TFIID components.
source: The anti-TAF11 co-IP from nuclear extract, in contrast, contained all TFIID components.
evidence: This is demonstrated by co-IP experiments shown in Figure 5.

claim: NSAF analyses of several distinct anti-TFIID IPs from nuclear extract indicate that less than half of the nuclear TFIID specimens appear to contain stably bound TBP.
source: Surprisingly, normalized spectral abundance factor (NSAF) (Zybailov et al., 2007) analyses of several distinct anti-TFIID IPs (i.e. anti-TAF1 and anti-TAF7) from NE indicate that less than half of the nuclear TFIID specimens appear to contain stably bound TBP, implying considerable dynamics in TBP association with TFIID in the nucleus, possibly regulated by TBP containing TFIID submodules such as TAF11/TAF13/TBP.
evidence: This is demonstrated by NSAF analyses of co-IP experiments shown in Figure 5.

claim: There is considerable dynamics in TBP association with TFIID in the nucleus, possibly regulated by TBP containing TFIID submodules such as TAF11/TAF13/TBP.
source: Surprisingly, normalized spectral abundance factor (NSAF) (Zybailov et al., 2007) analyses of several distinct anti-TFIID IPs (i.e. anti-TAF1 and anti-TAF7) from NE indicate that less than half of the nuclear TFIID specimens appear to contain stably bound TBP, implying considerable dynamics in TBP association with TFIID in the nucleus, possibly regulated by TBP containing TFIID submodules such as TAF11/TAF13/TBP.
evidence: This is inferred from the NSAF analyses.

claim: TAF11/TAF13 is unique in spanning the entire concave groove including the stir-ups of the saddle-shape adopted by TBP, with a solvent-excluded surface comparable to TATA-box DNA binding to TBP.
source: Careful inspection of the molecular modes by which different interactors engage the concave DNA-binding surface of TBP reveals that TAF11/TAF13 is unique in spanning the entire concave groove including the stir-ups of the saddle-shape adopted by TBP, with a solvent-excluded surface comparable to TATA-box DNA binding to TBP (Figure 6, Table 5).
evidence: This is demonstrated by structural comparison shown in Figure 6 and Table 5.

claim: TFIID is thought to exist in distinct structural states, based on cryo-EM analyses.
source: Holo-TFIID is thought to exist in distinct structural states, based on cryo-EM analyses (Cianfrocco et al., 2013; Louder et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: In the canonical state, TAF1 is proposed to associate via its TAND domain to the DNA-binding surface of TBP thereby inhibiting TBP/TFIID binding to TATA-box containing core promoter DNA.
source: In the canonical state, TAF1 is proposed to associate via its TAND domain to the DNA-binding surface of TBP thereby inhibiting TBP/TFIID binding to TATA-box containing core promoter DNA.
evidence: This is based on prior structural and biochemical studies.

claim: In the activated state, TFIID was proposed to undergo major conformational rearrangements, likely involving interactions with transcriptional activators, thus unmasking TBP to promote DNA binding stabilized by TFIIA initiating transcription.
source: In the activated state, TFIID was proposed to undergo major conformational rearrangements, likely involving interactions with transcriptional activators, thus unmasking TBP to promote DNA binding stabilized by TFIIA initiating transcription.
evidence: This is based on prior structural and biochemical studies.

claim: In TFIID, several distinct TBP/TAF interactions exist, which are formed to forestall unwanted TFIID/DNA interactions which could otherwise lead for instance to cryptic transcription initiation on genomic regions that do not contain promoter elements.
source: Our results suggest that, in TFIID, several distinct TBP/TAF interactions exist, which are formed to forestall unwanted TFIID/DNA interactions which could otherwise lead for instance to cryptic transcription initiation on genomic regions that do not contain promoter elements.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the results of the study.

claim: An alternative inhibitory TFIID state exists in which the TAF11/TAF13 HF pair blocks TBP from binding TATA-box containing promoter DNA.
source: In addition to the TAF1-dependent inhibited canonical state, we propose an alternative inhibitory TFIID state in which the TAF11/TAF13 HF pair blocks TBP from binding TATA-box containing promoter DNA (Figure 7).
evidence: This is a proposed model based on the findings of the study, illustrated in Figure 7.

claim: This alternative inhibited state may serve as a further point of transcriptional control, possibly depending on promoter context or additional gene regulatory factors bound.
source: This alternative inhibited state may serve as a further point of transcriptional control, possibly depending on promoter context or additional gene regulatory factors bound.
evidence: This is speculation based on the findings.

claim: In a given TFIID complex, the TAF1-dependent and the TAF11/TAF13 HF pair-dependent TBP-blocking activities are mutually exclusive, but they may compete with each other to ascertain full blocking activity.
source: Our results imply that, in a given TFIID complex, the TAF1-dependent and the TAF11/TAF13 HF pair-dependent TBP-blocking activities are mutually exclusive, but they may compete with each other to ascertain full blocking activity.
evidence: This is inferred from the competition experiments.

claim: The TAF11/TAF13 HF pair-dependent TBP binding/blocking activity is essential/required for normal TFIID function.
source: Interestingly, however, it appears that this TAF11/TAF13 HF pair-dependent TBP binding/blocking activity is essential/required for normal TFIID function, because when we interfered in the TBP binding through mutating the CTID, yeast growth was compromised at the non-permissive conditions.
evidence: This is inferred from the cell growth experiments with TAF13 mutants.

claim: TFIID integrity was not compromised by the mutations in TAF13 CTID.
source: At the same time, TFIID integrity was not compromised by the mutations.
evidence: This is demonstrated by co-IP experiments.

claim: Transcription activators and chromatin remodeling factors may direct inhibited TFIID to specific promoters, which could be poised to be transcribed by histone H3K4 trimethylation, and alleviate the TBP-blocking through TAF-interactions or by TAF-chromatin mark interactions.
source: Transcription activators and chromatin remodeling factors may direct inhibited TFIID to specific promoters, which could be poised to be transcribed by histone H3K4 trimethylation, and alleviate the TBP-blocking through TAF-interactions or by TAF-chromatin mark interactions.
evidence: This is speculation based on the findings.

claim: Once TFIID is brought to a promoter by interactions with transcription activators and positive chromatin marks (i.e. histone H3K4me3), DNA and TFIIA together may synergize to liberate the TATA-box-binding surface of TBP from the inhibitory TAF-interactions.
source: Alternatively, it is conceivable that once TFIID is brought to a promoter by interactions with transcription activators and positive chromatin marks (i.e. histone H3K4me3), DNA and TFIIA together may synergize to liberate the TATA-box-binding surface of TBP from the inhibitory TAF-interactions.
evidence: This is speculation based on the findings.

claim: The existence of discrete TFIID subassemblies containing a subset of TAFs, such as nuclear core-TFIID and the TAF2/TAF8/TAF10 complex present in the cytoplasm, provides evidence that holo-TFIID may be assembled in a regulated manner in the nucleus from preformed submodules.
source: The existence of discrete TFIID subassemblies containing a subset of TAFs, such as nuclear core-TFIID and the TAF2/TAF8/TAF10 complex present in the cytoplasm, provides evidence that holo-TFIID may be assembled in a regulated manner in the nucleus from preformed submodules (Bieniossek et al., 2013; Gupta et al., 2016; Trowitzsch et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Cytoplasmic TAF11/TAF13 building block did not contain detectable amounts of TBP, suggesting that trimeric TAF11/TAF13/TBP, within TFIID or as a discrete TFIID submodule, would be formed in the nucleus.
source: Note, however, that this cytoplasmic TAF11/TAF13 building block did not contain detectable amounts of TBP in our experiments, suggesting that trimeric TAF11/TAF13/TBP, within TFIID or as a discrete TFIID submodule, would be formed in the nucleus.
evidence: This is inferred from the co-IP experiments.

claim: Cytoplasmic TAF7/TAF11/TAF13 may represent an assembly intermediate toward a TAF1/TAF7/TAF11/TAF13/TBP module.
source: We speculate that cytoplasmic TAF7/TAF11/TAF13 may represent an assembly intermediate toward a TAF1/TAF7/TAF11/TAF13/TBP module, which may integrate into a core-TFIID and TAF2/TAF8/TAF10 containing '8TAF' assembly (Trowitzsch et al., 2015) in the formation pathway to the complete nuclear holo-TFIID complex.
evidence: This is speculation based on the co-IP results.

claim: In the putative TAF1/TAF7/TAF11/TAF13/TBP module, TBP would be tightly bound to either TAF1 or TAF11/TAF13, which could serve to ascertain that this putative TFIID submodule is efficiently blocked from any potentially detrimental interactions with DNA until holo-TFIID formation is completed.
source: In this TAF1/TAF7/TAF11/TAF13/TBP module, TBP would be tightly bound to either TAF1 or TAF11/TAF13, which could serve to ascertain that this putative TFIID submodule is efficiently blocked from any potentially detrimental interactions with DNA until holo-TFIID formation is completed.
evidence: This is speculation based on the findings.

claim: TFIID-type complexes may exist which do not contain TBP.
source: Strikingly, stoichiometry analyses carried out by NSAF calculations of our nuclear anti-TAF IPs indicated that TBP was only present in less than half of the TFIID specimens, when compared to TAF1 or TAF7 for example, suggesting that TFIID-type complexes may exist which do not contain TBP.
evidence: This is inferred from the NSAF analyses of co-IP experiments.

claim: TBP is thought to be highly mobile structurally in the context of holo-TFIID, with recent cryo-EM studies predicting large-scale migration of TBP within distinct TFIID conformational states.
source: TBP is thought to be highly mobile structurally in the context of holo-TFIID, with recent cryo-EM studies predicting large-scale migration of TBP within distinct TFIID conformational states (Cianfrocco et al., 2013; Louder et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: The observations point to an additional level of compositional TBP and/or TAF dynamics in TFIID formation, raising the interesting possibility that the accretion of TBP in holo-TFIID may be regulated by partially assembled nuclear TFIID building blocks including for instance the TAF11/TAF13/TBP complex.
source: Our observations point to an additional level of compositional TBP and/or TAF dynamics in TFIID formation, raising the interesting possibility that the accretion of TBP in holo-TFIID may be regulated by partially assembled nuclear TFIID building blocks including for instance the TAF11/TAF13/TBP complex we identified.
evidence: This is speculation based on the findings.

claim: TFIIAs-c crystallized during purification.
source: We stored highly purified TFIIAs-c at 4⁰C, and observed the formation of needle-shaped crystals in the storage buffer after several weeks.
evidence: This is an observation made during the study.

claim: The 2.4 Å crystal structure of TFIIAs-c was determined.
source: We improved the crystals manually and determined the 2.4 Å crystal structure of TFIIAs-c (Figure 1B, Figure 1—figure supplement 1, Table 1).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, shown in Figure 1B and Table 1.

claim: The crystal structure revealed a virtually identical conformation of unliganded TFIIAs-c as compared to TFIIA in the TFIIA/TBP/DNA complex.
source: The crystal structure revealed a virtually identical conformation of unliganded TFIIAs-c as compared to TFIIA in the TFIIA/TBP/DNA complex.
evidence: This is demonstrated by structural comparison shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: The crystal structure highlighted the importance of the connecting loops introduced in TFIIAs-c in stabilizing the three-dimensional crystal lattice.
source: Moreover, the crystal structure highlighted the importance of the connecting loops we had introduced in stabilizing the three-dimensional crystal lattice (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: TFIIAs-c was active in a band-shift assay with TBP and adenovirus major late promoter (AdMLP) TATA-DNA similar to purified TFIIA using the classical refolding protocol.
source: TFIIAs-c was active in a band-shift assay with TBP and adenovirus major late promoter (AdMLP) TATA-DNA (Figure 1C) similar to purified TFIIA using the classical refolding protocol (Bleichenbacher et al., 2003).
evidence: This is demonstrated by band-shift assays shown in Figure 1C.
